newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S. Commerce Secretary in Chile for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce Secretary in Chile for trade talks.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley arrived in Chile on Saturday to try to reassure his sceptical hosts that the Clinton administration remains serious about bringing them into NAFTA.
Daley will meet President Eduardo Frei and other top Chilean officials for talks on trade and the North American Free Trade Agreement, which Chile still hopes to join.

Earlier in Argentina, Daley played down reports of tensions between the United States and the Mercosur trade bloc -- Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay -- on the speed at which to pursue a Western Hemisphere free trade pact.

Tensions came to a head at a meeting on Friday in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, where officials from across the Americas agreed to launch hemispheric trade negotiations in March 1998 but did not settle differences over the scope of the talks.

Daley may find common cause in Chile. Despite signing an "association agreement" with Mercosur last year, Frei's government has kept its distance from the pact because of disputes mainly with Brazil over tariff policies.

Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, due to meet Daley on Monday, said last week that Chile was not interested in becoming a full member of Mercosur and preferred to step up efforts to build a Free Trade Area of the Americas.
Chile has been officially the next-in-line to join NAFTA since President George Bush's term. President Bill Clinton in 1994 renewed the U.S. commitment to bring Chile into the pact.
But opposition in the U.S. Congress to fast-track authority for U.S. trade negotiators has prevented talks from getting underway, and Chilean patience is growing thin.

"The issue of fast-track and NAFTA is now entirely up to the Americans and I have nothing to say about it," Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said this week, reflecting Chilean pique with what is seen as U.S. dawdling on NAFTA.
Chile, with an economy growing at a steady seven percent a year, already has bilateral free trade agreements with the other two NAFTA members, Canada and Mexico.
Daley is due to return to Washington on Tuesday.
